customConcept.name: Golden Corral (franchise)
customConcept.blurb: An all-you-can-eat buffet with a carving station, a chocolate fountain, rolls out of the oven all day, and a line at the door every Sunday after church.

state.circumstances: You own and run a Golden Corral franchise on a highway retail strip outside Raleigh, North Carolina, the city where the chain started in 1973. Golden Corral sets the buffet, the recipes, the suppliers and the brand; you set the door prices, the hours and the staffing, pay 4% of sales in royalty and 2.4% to the brand fund, and live with a building of 450 seats that has to be full on Sunday and Mother's Day to make the month.

features.name: The chocolate fountain
features.pitch: Warm chocolate running over a tiered fountain, with strawberries, marshmallows and pretzels to dip.

features.name: The carving station
features.pitch: A cook carving sirloin, turkey and ham to order under the heat lamps.

features.name: The party room
features.pitch: A private room for birthdays, church groups, teams and reunions, booked through group sales.

setting.name: Highway retail strip, Raleigh suburbs
setting.desc: A freestanding building with a big parking lot off a four-lane road, near a Walmart and three churches. Families, retirees, church groups after Sunday service, road crews at lunch, and every birthday in the county.

ev.text: Mother's Day: the line ran out the door and round the building from eleven until four.
Thanksgiving Day, one of the biggest days of the year: turkey carved non-stop from open to close.
Military Appreciation Night: a free dinner for every veteran and service member who came in. The room was full and the local news came.
An ice storm closed the roads for two days.
A viral video of a messy buffet line at another Golden Corral made the rounds, and the locals asked about yours.

log.text: You own and run a Golden Corral franchise on a highway retail strip outside Raleigh, North Carolina, the city where the chain started in 1973. Golden Corral sets the buffet, the recipes, the suppliers and the brand; you set the door prices, the hours and the staffing, pay 4% of sales in royalty and 2.4% to the brand fund, and live with a building of 450 seats that has to be full on Sunday and Mother's Day to make the month.

world.notes: Golden Corral is a buffet chain founded in 1973 in Fayetteville, North Carolina, with its headquarters in Raleigh; it had 348 restaurants in the latest year its franchise disclosure document reports, almost all franchised. The 2026 FDD (issued 27 April 2026) reports, for 263 franchised restaurants in metro markets in 2025, average gross sales of $4,923,317 (median $4,659,201) and average operating income of $1,092,235 before royalties, brand fund and occupancy; the royalty is 4% and the brand fund 2.4%. The buffet items here are all on Golden Corral's own nutrition list, which covers more than 1,300 items across the chain; soft drinks are Coca-Cola products and are sold separately from the buffet. Door prices vary by restaurant because franchisees set them: the ones here ($12.49 weekday lunch, $18.49 dinner averaged across weekday and weekend, $13.49 weekend breakfast, $8.99 kids) are typical of what 2026 price trackers report, not a menu this restaurant publishes. Weekend breakfast runs through the brunch programme. Golden Corral's Military Appreciation Night, a free dinner for veterans and service members every November since 2001, is real. The location, staff names, seat count, rent and local events are invented or estimated.

menu.identity: Golden Corral's endless buffet: pot roast, fried and Bourbon Street chicken, carved meats, a salad bar, yeast rolls and a dessert bar with a chocolate fountain.

team.name: Denise Whitaker
team.bio: General manager. Came up from the dessert bar twenty years ago; knows which church lets out when and staffs the Sunday rush to the minute.

team.name: Luis Ortega
team.bio: Kitchen manager: runs the hot line, the grill on steak nights and the carving station, and trains every new cook on the pot roast.

team.name: Tasha Greene
team.bio: Assistant manager on the evening shift, closing and counting the drawers.

team.name: Earl Simmons
team.bio: Bakery lead: yeast rolls and biscuits through the day, and the dessert bar.

franchise.rules: Golden Corral Franchising Systems sets the buffet, the recipes, the approved suppliers, the equipment and national advertising; the franchisee sets door prices, hours and staffing, and must keep to the brand's operating and sanitation standards. The royalty is 4% of gross sales and the brand fund 2.4%, contractually up to 6%.
